input_text: Angela is suing Harold for defamation. To prove that Harold knowingly spread falsehoods about her, Angela introduces evidence of Harold admitting to his friend that his statements about Angela were all lies.

extraction.input_text: Angela is suing Harold for defamation. To prove that Harold knowingly spread falsehoods about her, Angela introduces evidence of Harold admitting to his friend that his statements about Angela were all lies.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The statement was made out of court.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) defines a statement as oral, written, or nonverbal conduct intended to be a communication.
FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: that his statements about Angela were all lies

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Harold knowingly spread falsehoods about her

arguments.text: The statement is offered for a non-hearsay purpose: to show Harold's state of mind and knowledge.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) excludes statements offered for purposes other than proving the truth, such as to show the declarant's state of mind or knowledge.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Harold knowingly spread falsehoods about her

arguments.text: The statement qualifies as a party-opponent admission under FRE 801(d)(2).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2)(A) excludes statements offered against an opposing party and made by that party in an individual or representative capacity.
